Then Gadadhara with yellow robes and four hands quickly came there and called Prahlada. The son of Hiranya Kashipoo, Prahlada, seeing the Lord of Lakshmi, four armed, Narayana with lotus and disc in His hands come there, bowed low, and, with folded hands, began to speak to him with great devotion.

O Deva of the Devas! You are the Lord of the universe and devoted to your devotees. O Madhava! I have fought for full one hundred Deva years; still I have not not been able to defeat these ascetics. I do not know why. I am surprised at it.

Vishnu said O Forgiving One! These two Rishis Nara Narayana are, the perfect ascetics, self controlled and born of my Amsas. Therefore you have not been able to defeat them. What wonder is there! O king! Better go now to your Patala and keep your steadfast devotion on me. O Intelligent one! Do not quarrel any more with these two ascetics.
Vyasa said O king! The Daitya king Prahlada then advised by Vishnu went out of that place with his Asura followers; and the two
Nara Narayanas began again to practise their Tapasyas.
Here ends the Ninth Chapter of the Fourth Book of Shri Mad Devi Bhagavatam, the Maha Puranam; of 18,000 verses, on the fight between the Rishis and Prahlada by Maharshi Veda Vyasa.

sections.label: The Curse on Vishnu by Bhrigu
sections.name: Chapter 10

verses.en: Janamejaya said O Son of Parashara! There has arisen a great doubt in my mind on hearing just now your words. These Nara Narayana are the two sons of Dharma; they are ascetics, calm and quiet, the Amshas of Vishnu; they reside in a holy place of pilgrimage! They are filled with the Sattvic qualities, subsisting always on roots and fruits of the forest, the highsouled hermits and truthful. How were they addicted to such warfare? Why had they left their invaluable asceticism? And with what object were they fighting for full one thousand Deva years with Prahlada.
What was the end, O Muni, of their fight with Prahlada? Kindly explain to me in detail the cause of this warfare.

Women, wealth or any other worldly object can be the cause of any quarrel or fight amongst any persons; but, in this case, the two ascetics had none of these; how then this idea of fight sprung within their minds.

And why did they practise such severe austerities? Was it that they had to overpower others, or enjoy pleasures themselves or to reach Heaven that they practised tapasya? What fruits did they eventually obtain from such penances?
They became very lean and thin through their asceticism; still how could they fight full one thousand Deva years without getting fatigued.
They were not entangled in this fight for kingdom, or wealth or for women or for any other worldly object; then why did they fight with the high souled Prahlada?
Having no attachment for any worldly object nor any desire to gain any thing therefrom, why did they engage themselves so thoroughly, in such pains giving battle?
Intelligent persons always do works leading to bliss; they never do painful works; this is the long standing rule of the world.
The two sons of Dharma were the Amshas of Hah, all knowing and adorned with all qualities; why did they fight, subversive of religion?
O Maharshi! Even the dull and stupid persons in the world won't go to these deadly battles leaving asceticism and samadhi, leading to the purification of all desires.
I have heard that Yayati, the Lord of the earth was dropped from Heaven to this world, owing to his Ahamkara, though he was a virtuous king devoted to charities and sacrifices.

No sooner Yayati, said the king did Ashvamedha sacrifice, etc., with Ahamkara, egoism, he was dropped by Indra with thunderbolt in his hands. So one can see that, without Ahamkara no fight can occur. The ascetics had no bodily strength; therefore if they had to fight, it is through the waste of their Tapasya that they could do so.

Vyasa said O king! The all knowing sages that have realised the truth or Dharnna declare the threefold Ahamkara arising out the Sattvic, Rajasic and Tamasic qualities respectively to be the causes of this world.
How, then, can these two Munis being embodied forego their Ahamkaras? Without any cause, no actions follow; this is quite certain.
Tapas, charities, sacrifices all originate from the Sattvic qualities. And quarrels arise from the Rajasic or Tamasic qualities.
All arise from Ahamkara, whether good or bad; this is quite certain.
There is no other thing that enchains a soul than this Ahamkara.
It is out of Ahamkara that this Universe is created: how can it be then free from it?
O King! Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshha, even these are with Ahamkaras. Then how can you expect other ordinary Munis to be free from it?
Encased with Ahamkara, this Universe is rolling. Births and death occur repectively through this Karma.
O Lord of the earth. The Devas, birds and men are revolving in this world like the wheel of a chariot.
In this wide world who can count how many Avataras Vishnu had to take in all sorts of wombs, good or low.
Ordained by the Lord of the Universe, Narayana Himself had to take the Fish, Tortoise, Boar, Man Lion and the Dwarf incarnations.
Vasudeva Janardana the Lord, had to undertake countless Avataras births in this world.
In the Vaivasvata manvantara, the Avataras of Bhagavan Hari are being mentioned to you. Hear!
The all pervading Lord of the world, the God of the Gods, had to take several incarnations in this world, owing to the curses inflicted by Bhrigu.
The king said There has now again arisen another fresh doubt, why was Vishnu cursed by Bhrigu Muni?
O Muni! What injury did Hari commit to that Muni, and whereof the Muni Bhrigu cursed him.

Vyasa said Hear, O king! the cause of the curse; I will narrate to you. In days of yore, the king Hiranyakasipu, the son of Kashyapa often quarrelled with the Devas; owing to this incessant warfare, the whole universe was much alarmed and perplexed.
And when Hiranyakasipu was slain by the Man-Lion incarnation, Prahlada, the tormentor of the foes, continued his enmity towards the Devas and began to annoy them.
Thus one hundred years dreadful battle occurred between the Devas and Prahlada, to the astonishment of all.

O king! The Devas fought very hard and were victorious. Prahlada was defeated and was sorely grieved. Hearing that the Eternal Religion is the best, he handed his kingdom over to his son Bali and went to the Gandhamadan hill to practise tapasya.
The prosperous Bali, too, on gaining his kingdom, began to quarrel with the Devas and the war thus went on. Ultimately the powerful Indra and the Devas defeated the Asuras.

O king! Indra, of unequalled prowess, with the aid of Vishnu, deprived the Daityas of their kingdom. The defeated Daityas took refuge of their family spiritual guide Shukracharya and addressed him thus, O Brahmana! You are endowed with your fiery strength of Tapasya and you are now powerful; why are you not lending your helping hands to your Daitya followers. O foremost of the councillors. If you do not help us and save us, we will not be able to stay in this earth and will soon have to go down to Patala.

Vyasa said Thus addressed by the Daityas, the very kind hearted Shukracharya said, O Daityas! Do not be afraid; I will protect you by my fire of strength and vigour; and help you with sound counsels and medicines. Be brave and energetic and cast aside your mental agony and sorrow.

Vyasa said O king! The Daityas became fearless under the patronage of Shukracharya. The Devas had their spies and knew all about these. They held councils with Indra and settled that before the Daityas had time to dislodge us from our Heaven with the mantra of Shukracharya, we will speedily go and attack them. Thus attacked all on a sudden, they will all be slain by us and we will drive them down to the Patala.
Thus forming their resolves, with fully equipped arms and weapons, they went out of rage to fight with the Daityas and orderd by Indra and aided by Vishnu, they began to kill the Demons.
When the Devas were thus slaying the Demons, they got very much terrified and exclaimed “O Lord! Protect us! Protect us!” and took the refuge of Sukra.

Shukracharya, seeing the Daityas very much perplexed and distracted, at once cried aloud out of the influence of his Mantra “No fear, no fear,” Then the Devas on seeing Shukracharya left the Daityas and fled away to their own places.
Here ends the Tenth Chapter of the Fourth Book of the Maha Puranann, Shri Mad Devi Bhagavatam, of 18000 verses by Maharshi Veda Vyasa on the curse on Vishnu by Bhrigu.

sections.label: Shukra’s Going to Mahadeva to Get the Mantra
sections.name: Chapter 11

verses.en: Vyasa said When the Devas retired from the battlefield, Shukracharya addressed the Demons thus O best of the Demons! Please hear, what had been told to me by Brahma in days of yore.
Janardan Vishnu is coming here to slay all the Demons, He killed before Hiranyaksha, the king of the Asuras, in His Boar incarnation.
He killed Hiranyakasipu by assuming His Man-Lion appearance; now too, he will kill all the Daityas, no doubt, with great enthusiasm.

Now my mantra force will not be of any avail before Shri Hari. And without my help you will not be able to conquer the Devas. Therefore, O Demons, wait for some time for me; I will start today to the presence of Shiva Mahadeva to obtain from him the Mantra Shakti.
I will return, as early as possible, getting the Mantra from Shri Mahadeva; and with the help of the power of those great Mantras I will be able to protect you thoroughly.
The Daityas said O best of the Munis! We are now defeated and our forces are well nigh exhausted; how will we be able to stay on this earth and expect your return for so long a time?
Those who were of great strength amongst us, they all are slain; now we are left very few in number. In this crisis it is not advisable
and auspicious for us to remain here in this battlefield.
Shukracharya said Better you all stay here until I return, getting the requisite Mantra; remain peaceful and engaged in asceticism.

The heroes apply one or other of the following four measures conciliation, alliance, gifts and bribery, partitions and sowing dissensions and punishment or open attack according to the conditions of time, place strength and circumstances.

Intelligent and well wishing persons do serve their enemies even in time of distress; but no sooner they find that their strength and army have increased, than they try at once to kill all their enemies.
Now, therefore, pretend your meekness and allegiance and adopt peace and remain in your own place until my arrival.
O Demons! I will come back with the Mantra from Mahadeva. I will fight again with the Devas, by that veritable mantra power.
O king! Thus firmly making up his mind to have the Mantra, Shukracharya went to Mahadeva.
The Danavas sent Prahlada to the Devas for conciliation. The Devas regarded Prahlada truthful and they all trusted on him.
Prahlada with Asuras addressed thus the Devas with gentleness and humility.
O Immortals! We all have abandoned our weapons and armour. Now we desire to wear barks of trees and practise asceticism.
The Devas took Prahlada's words to be true and deserted from further fight; were freed of anxiety and felt all delighted.
On the Daitya’s leaving their weapons, the Gods desisted from battle, went to their respective places and freely gave themselves up to pleasure and amusements.
The Daityas controlled themselves and practised asceticism in the Kashyapa’s hermitage, expecting the return of Shukracharya.
Shukracharya went to Kailasa and made respectful obeisance to the God Mahadeva. Mahadeva enquired of the cause of his coming.
Shukracharya said 1 ask for Mantras, O Deva! from you that are not possessed by Brihaspati, for the defeat of the Devas, and the victory of the Asuras.
Vyasa said On hearing his words, the all-knowing Shankara Shiva began to think what He would do in this matter.
Certainly, this is with the revengeful object of attacking the Devas, for their defeat and for the victory of the Asuras that this Muni has come.
The Devas ought to be protected by me; thus thinking, Shankara Maheshvara advised him an entirely difficult tapasya to practise.
Full one thousand years he would practise tapasya with feet upwards and head downwards, he will have to inhale the smoke of burnt husk. Then he will get the Mantra and his desires will be fulfilled.
That would be done; thus saying to Shankara, Shukracharya practised that excellent vow, peaceful and inhaling the smoke of husk to get that Mantra.
The Devas came to know that Shukracharya is practising his vow and the Daityas have become arrogant. They then counselled.
And came to the conclusion, took up weapons and arms and went to the Daityas, ready to fight.
The Daityas, seeing the Devas dressed in armour and holding weapons and coming from all sides, became very much afraid and anxious.
The Daityas, seeing this all on a sudden, were attacked with fear and began to address the Devas, proud with their army, in words, full
of good meanings and morals.

O Devas! We have abandoned our arms; we are now armless; our spiritual guide is in his tapasya, you gave us words of fearlessness; why then you have come now dressed in full armour and with armies to kill us.
O Devas! Where is your truth. And where is your religion acccording to Shruti? It is stated in Shruti never to kill the weaponless, the fear stricken, and the refugees.
The Devas said You sent your good Shukracharya, out of pretence to acquire the Mantras; your asceticism is veiled under a deceitful object. Therefore we will fight with you certainly.
Be ready now and dress yourself with your arms and ammunitions, “Lo! Whenever you get any loop hole in your enemies, catch hold of it and kill your enemy.” This is the eternal religion.
Vyasa said On thus hearing the reply from the Devas, the Daityas after consideration quitted that place and fled away with terror.
And they took refuge under the Shukracharya’s mother. She saw the Daityas very much fearstricken and at once guaranteed to them protection from fear.
The mother of Kavya Shukracharya said Don’t fear; don’t fear; cast away fear. O Danavas! In my presence, no fear can overtake you.
The Asuras on hearing her words were free from anxiety and pain and remained in that hermitage, in no way now bewildered or agitated, though they had no arms.

Here the Devas, seeing the Daityas flying away, pursued them and entering the hermitage were ready to kill the Daityas, not taking into account what strength they gained there. The mother of Shukra warned the Devas not to kill; but, inspite of her hindrance, they began to slay the Daityas.
Seeing the Daityas thus attacked, the mother was furiously irritated and told them she would make all of them overpowered by sleep by her tapas strength, clarified intellectual force.
note: ls it by the asphyxiating gas? Or, by poisonous vapours or liquids?

verses.en: So saying she sent the Goddess of sleep who at once overpowered the Gods and made them all lie down on the grounds senseless. Indra with the other Devas lay there dumb, and miserable.
On seeing Indra thus stupefied by sleep, the Bhagavan Vishnu told Indra to enter into His body. He would then carry him to another place and he will be better.
Indra entered into the Vishnu’s body; and, under His protection, he became free from sleep and fear. On seeing Indra thus sheltered by Vishnu and fearless, the mother of Kavya spoke.
O Indra! I will devour you with Vishnu today by my Tapas force. All the Devas will presently see all this and my extraordinary power.
N.B.: Is it by making the earth go down, causing a fissure, thus engulfing the whole army? Or by blowing them up? Or by showering jets of poisonous gas or hot water or vapour from all sides.
Vyasa said O king! No sooner the mother spoke thus, than both Indra and Vishnu were both stupefied under her magical spell, superior thought power, and a thorough learning of the art of warfare.
The Devas, seeing them very much overpowered and bewildered, were greatly struck with wonder; they became desperate and began to cry aloud.
Indra, on hearing the Devas cry aloud, told Vishnu, O Madhushudana! I am more bewildered in particular than yourself.
O Madhava! No need of any further consideration. Before this wretch, inflated with pride by her tapasya, burns us, better cause her death as early as possible.
When thus requested by Indra who was very much perplexed, Bhagavan Vishnu quickly remembered his Sudarshana disc, casting aside the thought that it is hateful to kill a woman.

The disc, the ever obedient weapon of Vishnu appeared instantly at his remembrance; and Vishnu, becoming angry as prompted by Indra held the disc in His hand, and, hurling it off on the Shukra’s mother, severed off her head quickly. The god Indra became very glad at this.
The Devas became free from sorrow, got very much pleased and heartily exclaimed victory to Hari and worshipped Him and began to chant His praises.
Indra and Vishnu then became free from all troubles; but they began to fear that Bhrigu (Shukra’s father) would curse them terribly and without fail.
Here ends the Eleventh Chapter in the Fourth Book of Shri mad Devi Bhagavatam, the Maha Puranam of 18,000 verses by Maharshi Veda Vyasa, on Shukra’s going to Mahadeva to get the Mantra.

sections.label: Bhrigu’s Curse and the Dialogue Between Shukracharya and the Daityas
sections.name: Chapter 12

verses.en: Vyasa said O king! On seeing Vishnu killing his wife, and thus committing a dreadful atrocious act, the Bhagavan Bhrigu was very sorry and began to tremble with anger and addressed Madhushudana thus.

Bhrigu said O Vishnu! You have done an extremely sinful act. O intelligent one! Knowing it, you have done so; what a great wonder! Nobody dreams of the murder of this Brahman’s daughter; and you have committed it in deed, black and white.

O Deva! The Maharshis declare you to be Sattvic, engaged in preservation; Brahma to be Rajasic (creator) and Shambhu Shiva to be Tamasic (destroyer). Why then is the contrary thing visible in this case?
Why have you become Tamasic? Why have you done this heinous crime? O Vishnu! The females are never to be killed; this is a known fact; then why have you killed this woman without any fault.

You have done a very execrable act. What shall I do to you? It is mete that I would curse you. O Great Sinner! You have pained me very much and made me very weary. I will not curse Indra. You always assume a deceitful appearance and behave like a black cruel serpent; your mind is all full of wickedness; I will curse you.
O Janardana. Those Munis who call you Sattvic are fools; I have seen today that your ways are exceptionally vicious and Tamasic.
O Vishnu! I curse you now to take frequent births, suffer very frequently in different wombs, in the earth and thus suffer the pains of remaining in the wombs.
O king! Therefore whenever religion subsides in the world, Bhagavan Vishnu incarnates frequently in this human world, due to the curse of Bhrigu.
The king said O best of the Munis! Did that Mahatma Bhrigu again marry and lead a householder’s life when his wife was thus killed by the lustrous disc Sudarshana.
Vyasa said O king! The sacrificer Bhrigu angrily cursed Hah and next took that severed head and quickly placed it over the body as before and said

O Devi! Vishnu has slain you today; I will make you regain your life just now. If I am acquainted with all the Dharmas and if I have practised these in my life and if I have spoken truth always, then dost thou regain your life by my religious merit. Let all the Devas witness my power and strength. If I know the True, if I have studied all the Vedas and if I have realised the Knowledge of the Vedas, then I, sprinkling your body with this cold water, charged with my mantras, will revive you.
Vyasa said O king! Sprinkled by the water by Bhrigu, his wife regained her life and rose up at once and felt herself glad and smiled.

All the persons and living creatures seeing her stand, as if awoken from her sleep, at once exclaimed from all sides “well done, well done!” thanked Bhrigu and his wife very much and highly praised them.
Thus seeing the fair complexioned wife regain her life through Bhrigu, Indra and all the Devas were very much struck with wonder.
NOTE Thought power and inhalation of some medicines might have revived her.

Indra then adressed the Devas Now the mother of Shukra has regained her life through Bhrigu; but when Shukracharya will receive the mantra after his severe tapasya, we do not know what terrible harm; he would do to us!
Vyasa said O king! Though the deep sleep that overtook Indra had now left him, yet he became very unhappy, remembering the severe asceticism of Shukra’s tapasya and his receiving mantras.
Thinking over deeply in his mind, Indra called his daughter Jayanti and spoke to her with affection.

Go! Daughter! I have given thee over to the ascetic Kavya. Do this service for me, go to Kavya and help him in his asceticism and bring him under your control. By whatever acts the Muni be pleased, dost thou do at once and please him in every way and thus remove my fear.
The large-eyed beautiful Jayanti, hearing her father’s words, went to the hermitage and there saw the Rishi inhaling or drinking the smoke.
On seeing the body of the ascetic, and remembering her father’s words she brought the leaves of the plantain trees and began to fan him.
The intelligent Jayanti with no excitement used to bring the pure, clear, cool, and well scented water and place it, with great devotion, before the sage for his drinking.
NOTE: Here Indra bribed by giving away his daughter.

When the sun was over his head, she used to prepare some protection, with her clothes, from the sun and thus made the shade for him. Thus, in various ways, did she begin to serve the Muni, herself remaining steady in her religion.
She brought sweet and ripe fruits proper according to the Shastras and used to place them before him for his repast.
In the performance of his daily duties, she used to collect the Kusha grass of the span of thumb and fore finger, and flowers, white and yellow and placed them before him.
For the Muni’s bedding to lie down and sleep, she used to gather soft, green leaves and with them she used to keep his bed ready; and when the Muni laid himself down, she used to fan him gently.
Never did she exhibit for fear of curse, any gesture or posture calculated to disturb his mind.
The sweet-tongued, thin lady used to praise Shukracharya in pleasing and favourable terms.
When the Muni awoke, she placed water before him to wash his face and hands. Thus serving the Muni, did she stay in the hermitage.
The fear stricken Indra used to send messengers to fathom the mind of that self controlled Muni.
Thus did Jayanti serve for good many years the Muni, being void of anger and observing duly her celibacy.
In this way one thousand years passed duly, the God Mahadeva was very pleased and addressed Shukracharya that He had come to give him boons that he desire.

The God Mahadeva said Whatever there exists in this universe, whatever you see with your eyes and whatever cannot be described in words, you will be the lord of all these and the conqueror of all. There is no doubt in this. You cannot be killed by any creature; you will be the ruler of all beings and will be reckoned as the best of the Brahmanas.

Vyasa said The God Mahadeva disappeared then and there, after granting him the boons. Then Shukracharya saw Jayanti and said to herO lady of beautiful hips! Who and whose daughter art thou? What is the desire in your mind? What for you have come here? O one of beautiful thighs! what is your duty?
O beautiful eyed! I am very pleased with all that you have done for me. What do you want? O one of good vows! Ask boons from me; I will grant them even if they be difficult.
On hearing this, Jayanti’s face became bright with joy; she said: whatever I desire, you know that already by force of your Tapasya.
The Kavya said Your mental desires I know; still mention them yourself particularly; I will do good to you in any way you like; I am pleased with your services.
am the younger of my brother Jayanta. Father has given me over to you; I now like to live with you. Kindly fulfil my desires now. O
blessed one! You better take me and enjoy me according to Dharma. This is my desire.
Shukracharya said O thou of large and handsome hips! Better enjoy with me for ten years, according to your liking, without being visible to anybody.

Vyasa said Thus saying, Shukracharya went to his home and, according to religious observances, married Jayanti and lived with her for ten years under the shade of Maya and unobserved by anybody. On the other hand, the Daityas, hearing that Shukracharya returned home successful getting his desired Mantra, were very glad and went to his house to pay their respects to him. But Shukra was then living with Jayanti; hence the Asuras could not see him.
Then they got very much dejected, sorry and were drooped in spirits; they searched for him again and again.
Not being able to see Shukra under the shade of Maya, the Daityas were very sorry and got afraid and then returned to their own residences.

On the other hand, the Devas, knowing that Shukra was holding intercourses with Jayanti, Indra, the God of Devas, spoke to the Deva Guru Brihaspati. O Guru! Advise us what to do under the present circumstances and relieve us from the impending difficulties.
O Brahmana. Better go today to the Danavas and do that by which our honour may be maintained. You better put the Danavas
under some charm by your magical spell and think and do good to us.
On hearing Indra’s words and knowing that Shukra is now enjoying with Jayanti, Brihaspati went to the Danavas, putting on the appearance of Shukracharya.
Going to the Demons, he called on them very politely and sweetly. The Asuras said that Shukracharya had come in presence of them.
The Demons were very glad and bowed down before Shukracharya and could not make out that he was the false Shukracharya, under the mayic charm of Brihaspati.

Then the false Shukracharya asked the welfare of the Daityas and said 1 went so long for your good; I performed severe tapasya and satisfied the God Shambhu and acquired from him the Mantra, the sacred knowledge, and that I will frankly explain to you.
On hearing this, the Demons were very pleased and, knowing that the Guru had been successful, were filled with joy.
They saluted him with joy and began to live quietly and freely and without pains, having got rid of fear from the Devas.
Here ends the twelfth Chapter in the Fourth Book of Shri Mad Devi Bhagavatam, the Mahapuranam of 18,000 verses by Maharshi Veda
Vyasa on Bhrigu’s curse and the dialogue between Shukracharya and the Daityas.

sections.label: Cheating the Daityas
sections.name: Chapter 13

verses.en: The king said What did the intelligent Brihaspati do after he had assumed falsely the appearance of Shukracharya, and lived there as the spiritual guide of the Demons.

O Muni! Brihaspati is the Guru of the Devas; he also devotes his time in studying the Vedas; and is the ocean of all knowledge; he is the son of the Maharshi Angira and he is himself a Muni. Endorsed with all these good qualifications, how could he deceive the Demons

In all the religious Shastras, Truth is declared to be the essence of Dharma; and the Supreme Self is attained through Truth, so the wise sages say. How can we expect an ordinary householder to be true when such a man as Brihaspati takes recourse to falsehood with the Demons.

If one acquires, as one’s wealth, the whole Universe, still one does not require anything more than what is required in feeding one’s belly; how is it that Brihaspati could speak falsehood merely for the sake of his belly?

O Muni! The words sung by the ancient virtuous and respectable sages were true and had their corresponding objects denoted by those words; now they employed the term Shista meaning that there were virtuous, respectable persons as denoted by them. When Brihaspati can even commit such condemnable deceitful acts and speak falsehood, we can expect no virtuous respectable persons in the world. Where then do you find the Shista persons, denoted by the
word Shista, sung by the ancient sages? The word Shista is now meaningless!
The Devas are sprung from the Sattvic qualities, men from Rajasic qualities and birds, etc. from the Tamasic qualities.
When the Guru of the Immortals, the incarnate of Sattvic qualities, can become a liar, how can one expect those who are Rajasic or Tamasic to follow rigorously the truth?
Oh! This Triloki is all pierced with falsehood! Where is the Religion! And what will be the ultimate goal of all these creatures!
When Bhagavan Hari, Brahma, Indra and the best of the Devas when all can betake to pretext, fraud and trickery and show cleverness in them; what to speak of men!

O Giver of honour! When all the Devas, Vashistha, Vamadeva, Vishvamitra, Brihaspati and other ascetic Munis get themselves overpowered by lust and anger, when their intelligence gets destroyed by covetousness and avarice, when they are addicted to vices and are expert in fraud, pre-text and trickery, then what fate, alas! can you expect of Dharma and what help is there of any religious persons!
Alas! Indra, Agni, Moon, and Brahma when these get overpowered by the strong influence of lust, are in illicit love with others’ wives, where is the goodness and virtuous behaviour in this Triloki?
O Sinless One! To whom, then, can we look upon as our spiritual guide and our advice and law givers when all the Devas and Munis are corrupt with avarice?

Vyasa said O king! Be he Indra, Brihaspati, Brahma, Vishnu or Mahesha, whoever is embodied or will put on bodies, he will have to be in touch with the previously mentioned Ahamkara, and covetousness and other vices due to name and form.
O king! Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesha are all attached to sensual objects; and what improper and sinful actions there can be that cannot be committed by persons devoted to sensual objects!

It is through cleverness and fraud that any one devoted to sensual objects can easily make oneself as cleverly free from Maya; but when difficulty comes, then his trickery gets discovered and the respective qualities hidden in him are brought to bear their respective results. Know, then, the three qualities to be conjointly the cause of all these actions; as without any cause, no action gets visible.
These discrepancies in the case of Brahma and others are caused by the three qualities; their bodies are all created from Pradhan Mahat and the other 25 Tattvas (essences).
O king! Brahma and others are subject to death; then how can you doubt on other things? In advising others, everybody gives, as it were, good and virtuous advices; but the burden falls upon their
own heads; they fall off from their advices and act according to their hidden natures; then they yield to lust, anger, envy, egoism and fascination.
No one who is embodied can get rid of passions, born of the 3 qualities. O king! Thus the Triloki goes, is the saying of the Maharshis.

This Triloki, auspicious, inauspicious, mixed, never gets any serious change; its nature remains always uniform. See Bhagavan Vishnu sometimes practises severe asceticism; Indra, the lord of the Devas sometimes follows the practices of religious sacrifices. Again you find Vishnu Bhagavan, full of youth, fond of the Leela, enjoying the company of Rama in Vaikuntha; sometimes He is the ocean of mercy, is fighting dreadful battles with the Demons and being severely afflicted with their clusters of arrows; sometimes he gains victories, sometimes he gets defeat through the irony of Fate; thus he gets undoubtedly pleasures and pains. O king! some time Narayana draws all the worlds into his belly and takes his yogic sleep on the thousand headed serpent Shesha and again he gets himself awakened by Prakriti. O king! Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesha, Indra, the Devas, and Munis all of them, live up to the limit of their ordained time and when the time of Pralaya, the Universal dissolution, ends, this whole Universe, moving and nonmoving, again comes into existence as before; there is no doubt in this. O king, at the expiry of the ordained time, Brahma and all others will die, no doubt.

Again, in due course, Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesha and the other Devas come out and assume bodies and get all the passions, lust, etc., as ordained. O King! You need not be astonished; this Triloki always goes on accompanied by lust, anger, etc.

Persons free from lust, anger and other passions are very rare in this world. He who is afraid of this world does not marry, and thus being free from the attachments to any worldly object, becomes free and roams fearless. The Moon stole away the wife of Brihaspati and Brihaspati himself stole away the wife of his younger brother. Thus in this wheel of Samsara, all the creatures are ever passioned with attachment, avarice, etc.

The householder can never expect to obtain freedom. Therefore those who want to be free, should carefully relinquish the idea of the stability of the world and worship the Eternal Mother Full and Sat, Chit and Anandam.
This world, moving and unmoving, O Maheshani, rolls in madness, overpowered by Her Maya.
Intelligent persons worshipping Her, trample down the three qualities and become free. O king! No other Path exists for Freedom

Until one gets the Grace from the Maheshani, one never gets happiness. True mercy is not found anywhere else but from Her. Then one should worship the All merciful, being of pure heart. For Her worship leads to freedom, even in this body-hood.
He who getting a human frame fails to worship Maheshani, gets down from the highest rung of the ladder. This is my opinion.
This Universe, composed of the three qualities, is encompassed with Ahamkara and fastened to untruth; therefore
freedom can never be expected without the worship of That Potent Goddess, O Muni! O king! Renounce every worldly object and serve the Goddess Bhuvaneshvari; this is the highest duty of all.
The king said What did, then, the Devaguru do in the disguise of Shukracharya? And when did the real Shukracharya come there? O respected Muni! Speak on these points.
Vyasa said Please hear what the disguised Brihaspati in the shape of Shukracharya did afterwards.
The demons were made to understand clearly by Brihaspati; and then they took him for Shukracharya and placed implicit faith on him and began to think of him and him alone.

The Daityas, enchanted and deceived by the magic of Brihaspati, took now his refuge for acquiring the knowledge from him, since they mistook him for Shukracharya. Who is there that is not enchanted by the idea of gaining something?
On the other hand, when the term of ten years was over, Shukracharya, the real Guru of the Daityas, ceased enjoying Jayanti and began to remember his disciples, the Daityas.
He now began to think that “My disciples, the Daityas, are expecting every instant my return; and I would now go and see them, bewildered with fear.

They are my devotees and I ought to do such that they might not be afraid of the Devas.” And then he exclaimed to Jayanti, “O beautiful one! Let my sons take the shelter of the Gods; your term of ten years is today over; I now go therefore, to see my disciples; soon I will again come to you.”
52. “Be it so”, replied Jayanti, the best of those who know religion, “you can go where you like; I am not to destroy your Dharma.”

Hearing these words, Shukracharya went hurriedly to the Demons and saw the Devaguru Brihaspati sitting before them in the guise of Shukracharya. He was explaining to them the Jaina doctrines, compiled by himself and finding fault with the act of envy, taking revenge and killing and cursing the sacrifices, etc.
He was telling them “O Enemies of Gods! Truly, I am telling you words that will, no doubt, prove good to you. Non-killing is the highest virtue; even the enemies ought never to be killed.

It is the Brahmanas, addicted to enjoyments and pleasures of the senses, who want to satisfy their tastes and pleasures that are found in the Veda’s injunctions to kill animals; but there is no virtue higher than non-killing animals.”

O king! Shukracharya was perfectly astonished to hear Brihaspati, the Guru of the Devas, speaking against the Vedas and began to think that Brihaspati is certainly my enemy. My disciples have been duped by this cheat; there is no doubt in this.
Fie to Avarice! It is the seed of sin; very strong and the veritable gate to hell; Brihaspati, even, the Guru of the Devas, is speaking lies, bound under the influence of this heinous avarice!
Oh! What wonder is this that the Guru of the Devas, who is the promulgator of all the religious Shastras and whose word is accepted as the final decision, is now expounding the doctrines of atheists.
When Brihaspati can become the expounder of atheistic doctrines, impelled by covetousness what to speak of those whose minds are not pure and whose intelligence is not sharp?
This Deva Guru, though a Brahmin, is acting today like a rogue, wanting to take away all and is deceiving my disciples the Daityas, who have been confounded by his magic.
Here ends the Thirteenth Chapter in the Fourth Book of Shri Mad Devi Bhagavatam, the Mahapuranam of 18,000 verses on cheating the Daityas by Maharshi Veda Vyasa.

sections.label: The Daityas Getting Back Their
sections.name: Chapter 14

verses.en: S’UKRACHARYA
Vyasa said Thus arguing in his mind, Shukracharya smilingly said to the Daityas O Daityas! what for have you all been cheated by Brihaspati, the Guru of the Devas, in my guise.
I am Shukracharya; you are my disciples; this man is Brihaspati, wanting to serve the Gods. He has cheated you, there is no doubt in this.
This vain villainous person has assumed my form; do not put the least faith in his words. O Daityas! You are my disciples, follow unto me; leave this Brihaspati, vain and arrogant.
The Daityas, on hearing his words were struck with wonder at the resemblance of the two personages and came to the conclusion that “the person just come is the real Shukracharya.”

Then Brihaspati, the false Shukracharya explained to the Daityas in plain and enchanting words that “the second man just come is the Deva Guru Brihaspati; he has come here in my guise. His object is to cheat you.
He has come here to cheat you and serve the purpose of the Devas; do not believe in his words.
What knowledge I have acquired from the God Shambhu, I am teaching it to you; I will make you, no doubt, victorious in the battle with the Devas.”
Thus the Daityas, hearing the words of the false Shukracharya, thought the false one to be real and placed implicit reliance in his words.
The real Shukracharya, then explained them as much as he could; but the Daityas, owing to the magic of the false Shukracharya and to the wonderful effect of time, did not hear his words.

The Daityas thus convinced said to the real Shukracharya, “this man before us is our Guru for our welfare and enlightenment, he is the foremost religious Shukracharya; for ten years continuously he is giving us advices. You are not our Guru; you appear fictitious and false; you better leave this place and go away.”
The dull brained Daityas repeatedly told to Shukracharya the reproachful words and bowed down to the false Shukracharya, and, saluting, him, gladly welcomed him as their Guru.

The real Shukracharya, seeing the Daityas exceedingly attached to Brihaspati, the Guru of the Devas, and deceived by his words, cursed them out of anger and said: “As you have not taken my words though I have explained everything to you, you would lose your knowledge and get defeat.
As you have shown disrespect towards me, you will get the fruits of it at an early date and will then understand the deceitful behaviours of that Deva Guru.”
Vyasa said Thus saying Shukracharya hurriedly went away, infuriated with anger. Brihaspati was glad and remained there with his mind calm.

Brihaspati then knowing the Daityas cursed by Shukracharya, assumed his real appearance, left that place, and hurriedly returned to Indra. He began to say “I have undoubtedly succeeded in my undertaking; the Daityas have been cursed and left by me too. They are now helpless; so, O Good Suras! I have made them cursed, you would better now try to fight with them.”

Indra heard their Guru and became very glad; all the other Devas were glad and worshipped him. They held another cabinet, secret council, how to fight with the Daityas; and, then, all uniting together marched out in battle against the Asuras.
Seeing that the powerful Devas are marching towards them ready to fight and knowing their false Guru had fled, the Daityas became very anxious.
They told each otherAlas! We were enchanted by the Devaguru; the highsouled Shukracharya angrily left us; now it is our incumbent duty to satisfy him.
That vicious, dirty inside and pure outside, hypocrite Pundit Deva Guru, who used to go to his brother’s wife, has really cheated and has quitted us.
What are we to do now? where to go? How to satiate now the anger of Shukra so that he might be glad and help us.
Thus pondering over they all unitedly, shuddering with fear, again went to Shukracharya, keeping Prahlada in front of them.
They all bowed down at the feet of their Guru; Shukra remained silent; then, bursting with anger and with eyes red, told them.
You were all warned by me that you were being cheated by the Maya of Brihaspati; you did not take my word, as worth hearing, though unselfish, pure and leading to your welfare.
Rather you were influenced by him and infatuated with vanity, you insulted me; now you will have to bear undoubtedly the effects of that Karma.
You are now vitiated from the path of your welfare; go now where that disguised cheat resides for the welfare of the Gods; know me not to be a cheat like him.
Vyasa said O king! When Shukra finished saying his uncertain words, Prahlada clasped his feet and began to say thus
Prahlada said O our Guru Bhargava! Today we have come to you in a very distressed condition! O Omniscient! we are your disciples; we are your good sons; you ought not to quit us.
On your departure to get the Mantra, that hypocrite, vicious Brihaspati getting the opportunity, assumed your false appearance and cheated us.

Peaceful persons do not take any offence committed with ignorance; you know everything; you know very well that our hearts are devoted to thee and to thee alone. There is no need of telling anything further to you.
O Highly Intelligent One! By your Tapas, you know our inner minds and relinquish your anger. The sages say that the anger of the saints is not lasting.
O Muni! Water is naturally cool; when in contact with fire it gets hot; but, when the heat is removed, it gets cold shortly after.
O observer of good vows! Anger is like chandala; sages therefore quit it. Our prayer to you is that you leave your anger and be pleased with us.
If you do not quit your anger and if you make us overpowered with grief and sorrow, O blessed one! We, being abandoned by you, will go down to the Patala.
Vyasa said Bhargava heard Prahlada’s words and, with his intuitioned eye, came to see the proper state of affairs and was pleased and lovingly said.
You will not have to fear nor to enter into the Patala. You are my Yajamanas; I will certainly protect you all by my never failing Mantra power.
O knower of religion! What Brahma of yore told me, I am now telling you accordingly. Hear my truthful words, leading to your welfare.
Whatever is inevitable, doomed to pass, must come to pass, be it auspicious or inauspicious. No one is able in this world to go against the current of Fate.
Under the influence of Time you are now deprived of strength, therefore you will have to suffer defeat at the hands of the Devas and you will have to go once to the Patala.

Brahma said When your time to enjoy the sovereignty of the Triloki had come, you enjoyed the kingdoms of the Triloki with all its wealth and power. You attacked the Devas and, helped by Time, had been able to trample them under your feet and held your sovereignty for full ten yugas and enjoyed the pleasures without any hitch.
You will regain this kingdom in the Savarnik manvantara. Then Bali will come in your family as the grandson of Prahlada and will conquer the Triloki and will get name and fame throughout his kingdom.

When the Lord of Vaikuntha had incarnated as Vamana and stolen away the kingdom of Vali, then the Janardan Vishnu told Bali, the king of the Demons that “I have taken away your kingdom by pretext to serve the purpose of the Gods; you will become Indra, no doubt, in the coming Savarnika manvantara.”
Bhargava said According to the sayings of Shri Bhagavan Hari, your grandson Bali is now invisible to all creatures and is now passing away his time, very much terror stricken.
Being afraid of Indra, he is now staying in a lonely house as an ass. One day Indra on seeing him enquired of him, in various ways, the cause of his assuming that ass-body.

O Lord of the Daityas! You have always enjoyed pleasures of all the world; you are the ruler of the Daityas; you ruled over all the worlds; do you not feel shame now in thus assuming this ass body. The Lord of the Daityas, hearing him, spoke thus.

O Indra, there is nothing to be sorry in these matters. When the most powerful Vishnu can assume fish and tortoise incarnations, then what wonder is there that I by virtue of the force of Time, am now staying as an ass? When you had murdered a Brahman, you, too had hid yourself in the Manasa lake in the lotuses; similarly today distressed, I am staying here in this ass body.
O Indra! What sorrow or happiness can be to a person who is under the control of Fate. To him everything is alike; for whatever the Time wishes, It can act accordingly.
Bhargava said to Prahlada! Both persons Bali and Indra got enlightenment at the mutual conversations; and they went away to their places at their own will.
O Lord of the Asuras! I have narrated to you this story indicating how powerful is the Time. Know that the Devas and Daityas and all the human beings and this whole universe is under that Great Fate.
Here ends the Fourteenth Chapter in the Fourth Book of Shri Mad Devi Bhagavatam, the Maha Puranam of 18,000 verses on the Daityas getting back their Shukracharya, by Maharshi Veda Vyasa.

sections.label: The Truce Between the Daityas and the Devas
sections.name: Chapter 15

verses.en: Vyasa said O king Janamejaya! Prahlada was glad to hear the above words of the high souled Bhargava.
Knowing Fate to be the strongest, he addressed the Daityas Never, in this battle will victory be ours.

Then the victorious Dennons, infatuated with pride, told Prahlada What is Fate? We do not recognise it. We ought to fight. O Lord of us Fate reigns over those that are idle, not energetic. Has Fate any shape? Who has created it? Has anybody seen Fate? However let us gather strength and fight. You are very intelligent and all knowing; It is proper that you should take our lead in the fight.
O king! When the Daityas spoke thus, Prahlada, the great Destroyer of enemies, became the general and challenged the Devas to fight.
On seeing the Asuras in the battle field, the Devas, dressed with arms and weapons, began to fight with them.
For full one hundred years the dreadful battle was fought between Indra and Prahlada; on seeing this, the Munis were astonished.
O king! In this fearful battle, the Daityas with their general Prahlada, the followers of Shukracharya, got the victory.

Then Indra, advised by their Guru Brihaspati, began to remember the Goddess of the Universe, the Most High, the Giver of welfare, the Destroyer of all sorrows and calamities, and the Bestower of freedom, worship Her, and sing hymns to Her with great devotion.

Indra said Victory be to the name of the Goddess Mahamaya, the Eternal Mother, the Holder of the trident! Holder of conchshell, disc, club, and lotus, the Giver of “no fear.” Salutation to Thee, the Goddess of the Universe; Thou art the Supreme Heroine in everything that relates to force, that is described in the Shakti Darshana Shastras. Thou art the Ten Tattvas, Thou art the Mother, Thou art the Mahavidya (the Supreme Knowledge).
There are many Tattvas; here the ten tattvas are according to the Shakti Darshana. There are many Dharma Shastras. Here Shakti Shastra is meant.
The Tattvas are those ultimate substances into which these gross manifestations resolve. The tattvas are Mahavindu, Nada Shakti, Mishra Vindu, etc.

O World Mother! Thou art the Maha Kundalini (the great Serpent Fire); thou art the Everlasting Existence, Intelligence and Bliss; Thou art the Deity of the vital Fire (Prana); Thou art the Deity of the Agnihotra (maintenance of the Sacred Fire and an oblation to It);
Thou art the Holy Flame, burning always in the ethereal space in the Heart; Salutation to Thee!

Thou dwellest within the five Sheaths (the Annamaya, the Pranamaya, the Manomaya, the Vijhanamaya and the Anandamaya sheaths are the five sheaths here referred to). Thou art the Indweller of the Ananda maya kosa, Thou art of the nature of Puchchha Brahma, the end of Brahma. Thou art the Deity of all, the Ananda (bliss) unblown, O Mother! Thou art the Deity of all the Upanishadas.

O Mother! Be pleased unto us; we have become powerless; protect us, O Mother! we are defeated by the Daityas; O Goddess! Thou art endowed with all the powers. Thou art our Sole Refuge in this Universe, in times of distress, and Thou art the Only One, strong and capable to remove all our dangers.

O Goddess! Those who incessantly meditate on Thee are really happy and those that do not meditate Thee, their fear, and sorrows are never removed; those that want ultimate freedom from bondage and who meditate on Thee always; those pure souls, being free from Ahamkara, and free from attachment go, no doubt, beyond this ocean of world.

O World Mother! Thy prowess is ever manifested whenever protection is demanded; You always come forward and relieve the distressed; You are the great destroyer! Thou art the Time Incarnate of all these worlds; O Mother! We are fools; how can we appreciate your qualities.

Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesha, I myself, Sun, Yama, Varuna, Fire, Air, the high minded munis, Agama, Nigama, the Tantras and the Vedas, are quite unable to realise Your unequalled prowess; Salutation to Thy Feet.

Those are blessed that are devoted to Thee; They are the great souls; they always dive in the Ocean of Bliss, being always free from the fangs of this Samsara. Those that are not Your devotees, cannot cross this Ocean of Samsara, where the Birth and Death are the billows.

O Goddess! Those that are always fanned by the white chamaras and those that travel always in cars, they in their previous births worshipped Thee with various things; therefore they have acquired the effects of their meritorious deeds; this is my opinion.

Those that are always worshipped amongst the human beings, those that go on nice elephants, those that are surrounded by pleasures and enjoy the lovely companions of beautiful coquettish women, those that go surrounded by soldiers, O Goddess! I consider they worshipped Thee in their previous births, and they are now enjoying fruits of their past deeds.

Vyasa said Thus praised by Indra, the Goddess of the Universe with four arms hurriedly appeared there mounted on a lion Conchshell, disc, club, and lotuses were held by the beautiful eyed Goddess in Her four hands respectively, wearing a red apparel and ornamented with divine garlands.
The Goddess being pleased addressed the Devas with sweet words, “Cast off your fear. O Devas! I will see presently all about your welfare.”
Addressing the Devas thus, the Divine Mother nnounted on a lion, went hurriedly to the place where the demons were waiting, infatuated with pride.
All the Daityas with their general Prahlada saw the Goddess before them and were terrified and began to address each other “What are we to do now?”
This Chandika Goddess has come here to protect the Devas. She destroyed Mahishasura and Chanda Munda; it was She that killed, in days of yore, Madhukaitava with evil look.

Seeing the demons thus full of sorrowful thoughts, Prahlada addressed the Daityas “It is better not to fight but let us fly away all together.” Then the Daitya Namuchi told the Daityas ready to fly away “If you fly away, this World Mother will instantly kill you all with weapons in Her hands.
Do that by which we can protect us. Let us worship the Goddess of the Universe, and, getting Her permission, we will go this very day to the Patala.”
Prahlada said “I will worship the Goddess Mahamaya, the Creatrix, Preservrix and Destructrix of the Universe, the World Mother, and the Assurer of safety to Her devotees.”
Vyasa said Thus saying, the knower of the highest knowledge, Prahlada, the devotee of Vishnu, began to sing hymns with folded hands in praise of the Goddess, the Upholdress of the Universe.

I bow down to Thee, the incarnate of the mantra “Hrim” the Refuge of all, and within Whom this whole Universe, moving and unmoving, is appearing untruly as a snake is mistaken for a garland of flowers.
O Goddess! All these Universes, moving and unmoving, have sprung from Thee; Brahma, Vishnu and others are Creators, Preservers in name only; Thou hast created them all.
O Mahamaya! You are the Divine Mother of all! When You have created the Asuras and the Suras, how can you then see any difference between the Devas and the Daityas?
As a Mother makes no distinction between her good sons and bad sons, so You are not to make any difference between us and the Devas; this is our prayer to you.
O Goddess! You have been sung in all the Puranas as the World Mother; therefore, O Mother! We are your sons just as the Devas are.
O Mother! As they have got their interests, so we too have got our interests; therefore there is no difference between he Daityas
and the Devas. Therefore if anyone nnakes any difference, it is due to the subtle error.
O Goddess! As we are attached to wealth, wives, and other pleasures of the senses, so the gods are; O Goddess! How then can any difference exist between them and us.
O Mother! They are the sons of Maharshi Kashyapa; we also are his sons; Therefore you cannot have partiality for them before us.
O World Mother! In You no such difference is visible anywhere. Therefore do You here preserve equality amongst us both.
The Suras and Asuras all have sprung from the permutations and combinations of the 3 qualities! Then how the Devas being embodied can possess more qualities than us.
Every embodied soul possesses always cupidity, anger, covetousness; how then can one expect to remain without any quarrels with others.

We think that it is all sport with You to see our opinions different, rather contradictory, and it is You who got us involved in quarrels with each other and it is Your pleasure to witness how we fight against each other.
Sinless one! O Chamunde! Were You not so fond to see our fight, how then, we being brothers are at war against each other.
Certainly it is Your Divine Sport.
O Goddess! I know what is religion, I know who is Indra. It is the very idea to enjoy these sensual pleasures that is the only cause of our incessant quarrels.

O Mother! You are the Sole Ruler of this Samsara; no sensible man can carry out the words of a man who yearns for something, (i.e., O Mother, You are the only one that is desireless; so we can obey your words).
O Mother! Once the Devas and the Asuras conjointly churned the ocean. At that time Vishnu, on the plea of distributing the jewel, and the ambrosial nectar, incurred quarrels amongst them.

O Mother! You have made him the Preserver and Controller of the Universe and the Spiritual Guide of the world. And it was He who took away the Goddess Lakshmi, the beautiful lady amongst the Deva women.

Indra, the Lord of the Gods, took the elephant named Airavat, the flower Parijat, the Heavenly Cow yielding all desires, and the horse Uchchaishrava. Thus, through the desires and devices of Vishnu, they got the excellent things.

O! What a wonder is this that the Devas were considered holy persons, after they had committed such unholy acts; no doubt the Devas had done a very heinous crime. O Goddess! You can judge Yourself what is the just and unjust thing in this case.

What is Religion? And where is Religion? And what are the acts done by a religious man? What is uprightness, justice, and purity? You better examine which party has observed virtue? Who has shown uprightness, justice and parity? To whom victory and defeat are due? You are the only one capable to judge all these things.

Alas! Whom to tell all the conclusions arrived at in the Mimamsakas. If any one considers, one will find the world is the field of dissensions and quarrels; the argumentators look to the logical reasoning only; followers of the Vedas look to the rules and regulations only; these so called men of gross ideas they acknowledge that this world is created and preserved by the One only, and yet they quarrel amongst each other.

If there be One and only One Lord of this wide infinite Samsara, then why would there be differences and quarrels amongst each other? Why is there not seen any agreement in opinion and why do the Shastras differ and why are there so many differences in the opinions held by the knowers of the Vedas.

O Goddess! This whole Universe, moving and unmoving is selfish; hence arise so many differences between several opinions. There was no one unselfish in this world and there would be no unselfish persons born hereafter.

Look! The Moon stole away perforce knowingly the wife of Brihaspati; Indra, knowing what is religion stole away the wife of Gautama; Brihaspati enjoyed forcibly the wife of his younger; and also he outraged his elder brother’s wife in her pregnant state and cursed the boy in the womb and made him blind. What more to say

than Vishnu, all full of Sattvic qualities, severed perforce the head of Rahu. O Mother! Look to the case of my grandson Bali who used to pay due respects to all, who was the foremost amongst the virtuous, observer of rigorous truth, performer of sacrifices, liberal, peaceful, all-knowing. The pretender Hah, taking the form of a dwarf in his Vamana incarnation, deceived Bali and took away all his kingdoms. Alas! Still the intelligent good persons reckon the Deva Vishnu as the preserver of Religion. What a wonder! Those who are flatterers become victorious in this world; and defeat come to those that speak of Dharma.
O Goddess! You are the Mother of all the worlds; do whatever You like. But You should know that the Demons are all under Your protection; kill or save them as You like.
The Devi said O Demons! Leave you all the anger arising from this warfare and go without any fear to Patala and live there at your ease and happiness.
Better now wait on Time; whether you will get auspicious or inauspicious fruits for your deeds. Know whoever is desireless and unattached, to him happiness is always and everywhere.

Whose mind is avaricious. He does not get peace and happiness, even if he acquires the Triloki. Even, in the golden age, avaricious persons did not get happiness, though they acquired the fruits of their actions.
Therefore you get yourselves freed of your sins and obey My order and leave the earth and go down to the Patala.
Vyasa said On hearing the Devi’s words, the Demons obeyed and bowing at Her feet and preserved by Her, went to Patala.
Then the Devi disappeared; and the Devas went away to their own homes. Thus the Devas and the Daityas, abandoning their feelings of enmity towards each other, lived in peace.
O King! He who hears this fact, gets himself freed from all sorts of calamities and reaches the Highest Peace.

Here ends the Fifteenth Chapter in the Fourth Book of Shri Mad Devi Bhagavatam, the Maha Puranam of 18,000 verses, on the truce between the Daityas and Devas and on their departures with peace, by Maharshi Veda Vyasa.

sections.label: The Birth of the Several Avataras of Vishnu and Their Deeds
sections.name: Chapter 16

verses.en: Janamejaya spoke O best of Munis! How did Vishnu, of wonderful deeds, get his incarnation owing to the curse, cast on Him by Bhrigu? what were His different incarnations in different Manvantaras respectively? O Thou, well versed in religion! O Brahmana! Kindly narrate those sin-destroying deeds of Hah in His several incarnations, that are the source of happiness, peace and welfare to all humanity.
Vyasa said O king! Hear, I am narrating to you the incarnations of Shri Bhagavan Hah which He had in the several Manvantaras and in the several Yugas respectively.
I will tell you now, in brief, what forms He took and what deeds He did in the various incarnations.
In the Chakshusha Manvantara, the Bhagavan Hah took the incarnation of Dharma; and the two sons of Dharma, Nara Narayana, were widely celebrated in this world.
Then, in the present Vaivasvata Manvantara, under the reign of Vaivasvata Manu in the second Yuga, Bhagavan Hari incarnated as Dattatreya, in the shape of the son of Atri Rishi.
Anasuya the wife of Atri, was desirous to have, as her sons, the three Devas Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra; and in fulfilment of her
desires, the Devas took their births in her womb.
Anasuya, was foremost amongst the chaste and virtuous women and on her praying, Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra the Trinity at once agreed to become her sons.
Brahma was born as Soma, Hari was born as Dattatreya and Rudra was born as Durvasa.
In the fourth Yuga, the Bhagavan assumed the beautiful double form in one, the upper part resembling a lion and the lower part a human being to accomplish the noble purpose of the Devas.
It was to kill Hiranyakashipu that the Bhagavan Hari assumed this appearance, wonderful even to the Devas.
In the Treta Yuga, the superior and the best of all the Yugas, the Bhagavan incarnated as Vamana (the Dwarf), the son of Maharshi Kashyapa, to curb the power of Bali.
The Dwarf Hari took away by pretext, the kingdom of Bali, while he was performing a sacrifice and sent him down into the Patala (the lower regions).
Afterwards, in the nineteenth Yuga, known as the Treta Yuga, Shri Bhagavan Hari incarnated as Parashurama, very powerful and the son of Jamadagni Rishi.
He was very beautiful and graceful in his body, truthful and the conqueror of his senses. He extirpated the Kshatriya race and gave the whole world over to the high minded Rishi Kashyapa-
O king! He is the Parashurama, the sin-destroyer, the incarnation of Hah, and the doer of wonderful deeds.

After that the Bhagavan Hari incarnated as Rama, the son of Dasharatha. Next in the twenty-eighth Dvapara Yuga, He incarnated as the very powerful Arjuna and Shri Krishna, the Amshas of Nara Narayana. To remove the load of the earth, these two were born; and they fought deadly battles in the battlefield of Kurukshettra. O king! Thus the several incarnations of Hari arose, according to the requirements of Prakriti. O King! These three worlds are under the control of Prakriti.

Whatever the Prakriti wishes at any time. She can fashion the world in that way. And She does this incessantly in accordance with the Word Divine, the Highest Shakti, to please the Purusha, without any cessation.

In days of yore, the most ancient Bhagavan, the Highest, above all the qualities of Maya, formless, all pervading, difficult to be conceived, without any decay, self-supporting, without any want, created these worlds, moving and unmoving and He manifested Himself as the Trinity, Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesha in the shape of the three qualities Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, and which is called the Highest Prakriti.

This all auspicious Prakriti shines differently according to the differences in time and circumstances. This threefold Prakriti, the Great Enchantress of the world is creating, preserving the worlds and is destroying them at the end of the Kalpas.
O King! Whenever there takes place the union with this Prakriti, Brahma creates, Vishnu preserves, and the all-auspicious God Shankara destroys the worlds.
It was She That gave birth to Kakutstha, the best of the kings; and to conquer the Danavas, She placed him at a certain place.
O king! Thus all men controlled by the Great Law in this world, enjoy sometimes the pleasures, enjoy sometimes pains and thus exist in the world.

Here ends the Sixteenth Chapter in the Fourth Book of Shri Mad Devi Bhagavatam, the Mahapuranam of 18,000 verses, by Maharshi Veda Vyasa, on the Birth of the several Avataras of Vishnu and their deeds.

sections.label: The Questions Asked by Janamejaya
sections.name: Chapter 17

verses.en: Janamejaya said O Muni! You told before that the heavenly prostitutes sent by Indra in the hermitage of Nara Narayana became lustful and desired to live with Narayana only, whose heart was calm and quiet.
At that moment when Narayana was about to curse them, his brother Nara desisted him from taking that step.
Now I ask you what did that triumphant Narayana Muni do, in the critical juncture, when he was repeatedly asked by those prostitutes, sent by Indra, to satisfy their lust?
O Grand Sire! I am very eager to know the deeds of Narayana, leading to one’s freedom. Kindly describe in detail and fulfill my wishes.
Vyasa said Hear, O king! I am describing to you in detail, what that high souled son of Dharma did.
When Narayana Hah was ready to curse them, the Rishi Nara, seeing this, consoled him and desisted him.
Then the great sage, the ascetic son of Dharma, Narayana, leaving aside his anger, began to address them in sweet words with
countenance smiling.

O Fair women! We have determined to practise asceticism in this life; it does not therefore behove us to accept any wife; therefore shew your kindness unto us and go back to your Heaven. You would better think that those who know what is religion, they never desire to break the vow of another.
11.0 beautiful eyed ones! In the sexual pleasure, it is the delightful feeling of passionate joy that is requisite; and we are wanting in those feelings; then how can we effect that union?

No action can come out of no cause; this is all clear. The poets say that the sexual power and pleasure, is the feeling, the mental attitude that corresponds; and that is the only thing, that lasts. And we have no desire for that.
However my limbs are all very graceful, I am very fortunate and blessed in this world, otherwise how can I be the object of your sincere love towards me.
You all are very fortunate; therefore do now show this mercy unto me “do not break my vow.” I pray now that, in a subsequent birth, I may become your husband.

O large eyed fair women! In the twenty-eighth Dvapara Yuga, I will certainly incarnate on earth to effect the purpose of the Devas; then you all also would respectively incarnate as the daughters of kings and would also become my wives.

Narayana thus consented to marry them in some other next birth; and consoling them, made them go back to their Heavens. They also abandoned their mental disquietude and, on reaching back to Heavens, they explained everything to Indra.

Indra heard (from these heavenly women) what the two two Rishis did and saw before him Urvashi and other women created by Narayana from his thighs, etc., and began to extol the merits of the high souled Narayana.
Indra said O! How wonderful is the patience of the Muni?
What is the wonderful influence of his Tapas! Oh! He has created, by the sheer force of his Tapas, Urvashi and these fair women, unrivalled for their beauties, from his thighs.
The Lord of the Devas thus extolled his merits and became freed from his anxieties. The virtuous Narayana, too, devoted himself to the practice of his Tapasya.
O king! Thus I have described to you, in detail, all the wonderful accounts regarding Nara Narayana.

O Superior in the descendants of Bharata! These two Nara and Narayana afterwards incarnated themselves, due to Bhrigu’s curse as the two great heroes Arjuna and Krishna, to relieve the burden of the earth.
The king said O respect giving Muni! Now describe in detail the life of the Avatar Krishna and dispel my mental doubt.

O best of the Munis! Why were Vasudeva and Devaki, who were chosen by the very powerful Hah and Ananta as their parents, doomed to so many miseries and afflictions. Why had these parents to remain for good many years in the prison of Kamsa, who pleased directly by their Tapasya that Bhagavan Janardana.
Why did Krishna taking his birth at Mathura, go to Gokula? Also what was his object to go to Dvarka, situated in the ocean, when he killed the enemy Kamsa?
Also why did his father, mother and relatives, leave their old holy places of residences and go abroad to live in a wretched old country?

Why was the Yadu race destroyed by the curse from a Brahmana! How did Shri Krishna Vasudeva leave finally His body after He had relieved the burden of the earth and was about to enter into His Heaven? The evildoers of the earth were slain by Krishna and Arjuna, of unequalled prowess; but how was it, that those who plundered the wives of Shri Hah, were not at all punished by Him?

The great personages Bhisma, Drona, Kama, the king Valhika, Virata, Vikarna, Dhristadyumna, the king Somadatta were destroyed for relieving the burden of the earth; and the plunderers were acquitted! Kindly explain the cause of this.
How was it that those chaste and virtuous wives of Shri Krishna go into troubles at the latter end of their lives? There has arisen a doubt in my mind on this point.
Why did the virtuous Vasudeva leave his mortal coil owing to the death of his sons and why did he die an unusual death?
O best of Munis! The Pandavas were devoted to Krishna and they were religious; they had to suffer so many troubles!
Why was Draupadi so very unfortunate and she had to suffer so much miseries, and pains, who was born of Lakshmi from amidst the sacrificial place and from the altar.

Why did Duhshasan drag Her by Her hairs while She was in Her menstruation period, in the hall of audience and why was it that Sindhu Raj Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu, gave Her exceedingly mental troubles?
Why was it that Her five sons residing in Her house were killed by Ashvaththama? What was the cause that the son of Subhadra had to die in the battlefield?
Why did the king Kamsa kill the six sons of Devaki; and why was it that Shri Hah who was capable of averting the Fate did not at all prevent that?

What a wonder is this that in the matters of Brahmana’s curse toward the Jadavas, their being killed in the Prabhasa, the total extermination the Jadu race and the plundering of His wives, why did He allow Fate to do these great momentous things?
If He was the all-powerful God and He Himself Narayana, that why did He incessantly act like a slave towards Ugrasena.
N.B. - Ugrasena was the king of Mathura and father of Kamsa. He was deposed by his son; but Krishna after having slain Kamsa restored him to the throne.

All these bring doubt in our minds regarding Narayana Muni that His deeds are always like those of ordinary persons; why did his pleasures and pains resemble those of ordinary human beings? Were he God, why his actions were not Godly? (i.e., superhuman)
Therefore dost Thou describe in detail all the Divine Leelas (playful sports) done by Hah of superhuman powers in this world.
O Best of Munis! When one’s longevity expires, one dies; then I cannot understand what glory was manifested by Hah in killing the Daityas? For Fate Killed them; not Hah.
Was not the doing of Hari like a thief when he stole away the Lady Rukmini and fled quickly to his own place.
What did it mean when he fled to Dvarka city, and quitted his own highly prosperous town Mathura simply out of the fear of Jarasandha?
Did not anybody at that time recognise that he was Shri Bhagavan Hah? O Respected One! Were he Bhagavan, why did He hide himself in Vraja? Please explain the cause to me.
O Muni! These and many other doubts always exist in my mind; you are the best of the Dvijas and blessed; I pray, dost thou remove these doubts.

O best of Munis! Another doubt exists and is not dispelled and that is secret. Was not the taking of the five husbands by Panchali for herself shameful and despised by the society? The good manners and doings are always considered by the learned as the proofs of virtue. Why did those Pandavas, then, capable in every respect, do this thing like brutes?
And what did Bhisma do living like a Deva in this world? May I ask, was his act of producing two sons by a widow and thus preserving his line of ancestors worthy of his name?
The religious sanction advocated by the Munis “Procreate sons in any way whatsoever” is simply shameful. Fie to this religious sanction.
Here ends the 17th Chapter in the 4th Book of Shri mad Devi Bhagavatam of 18000 verses by Maharshi Veda Vyasa on the
questions asked by Janamejaya.

sections.label: The Devi Earth’s Going to the Heavens
sections.name: Chapter 18

verses.en: Vyasa said O king! Hear in detail the complete life and the deeds in the incarnation of Shri Krishna and also the various wonderful achievements by the Goddess of this universe.
Once on a time, the Earth was very much overburdened by the load of wicked kings and She was therefore very much afraid.
She then assumed the appearance of a cow and went to the Devaloka crying and very much dejected.
Indra, the lord of the Devas, asked her, O Vasundhare! What is the cause of your fear now? Who has troubled you? What afflictions are you merged in? Please tell me all these.

On hearing Indra’s words, the Earth exclaimed O Respect giver! When You have asked me, I am explaining to you the cause of all my afflictions and sorrows; at present I am overburdened with too much load.

Now is reigning in the earth Jarasandha, the king of Magadha, a very very vicious person. Thus the other Shishupal, the lord of the Chedis, the uncontrollable Kashiraj, Rukmi, the powerful Kamsa, the strong Naraka, the Sauvapati Shalva, the wicked Keshi, Dhenuka, and Batsaka all these are now in royal positions. O Lord of the Devas! These kings are all devoid of the least trace of virtue, quarrelsome

against each other, infatuated with vanity, and addicted to vicious deeds. These have become kings as if they were personified Yamas, the Lords of Death, and are constantly troubling me. I am now unable to carry their loads; where shall I go now? This great thought is constantly ailing me.

9-11.0 Vasava! What to tell! The Bhagavan in His Boar Incarnation is the cause of all these my afflictions; O Indra! These present troubles I am fallen into only through Him; for when the cruel Daitya Hiranyaksha; the son of Ka’syapa stole me away and drowned me in the great ocean, then it was Vishnu in his Boar incarnation that killed him and rescued me from the ocean and then kept me in this my stable position.
Had he not then lifted me up, I would have rested safe in the depths of Rasatala; O Lord of the Devas! Now I am quite unable to bear the load of these vicious persons.
O Surendra! The vicious twenty eight Kali is coming quickly in front. Thinking of His influence, it seems to me that I will be very troubled then and will have to go down to Rasatala.
Therefore, O Lord of the Devas! I am bowing down before Your feet, kindly relieve me of my burden and save me from these endless troubles.
Indra said O Earth! I cannot do anything for you. You better go and take refuge of Brahma. I am also going to Him. He will remove all your troubles.
Hearing Indra’s words the Earth hurriedly went to the realm of Brahma and Indra and all the other Devas followed Her; and all reached the Brahmaloka.

O King! The Grand Father Brahma saw the Earth coming to him and through the power of meditation, found out the cause of Her coming and said O Auspicious One! why are You crying? What troubles You have now? What wicked person has given You troubles.
The Earth said O Lord of the Earth! The vicious Kali is coming before; under Its influence the subjects will be horribly vicious; therefore I am very much afraid of this Kali.

In the beginning of this Kali Yuga, the ancient enemies, the Asuras have now incarnated on this earth as kings. They will be extremely wicked, quarreling against each other, and will be clever in stealing others’ things. There is no doubt in these.
O Grand Father! Now kill these vicious kings and relieve my burden. O Lord! I am very much troubled by the armies of these kings.
Brahma said O Goddess! I, too, am unable like Indra to remove your load. Let us go to that Vishnu, the Holder of the disc.
That Janardana will remove your burden. I thought of this well before and settled what to do.

Vyasa said Thus saying, the four faced Brahma, the Author of the Vedas, rode on His Hamsa Vehicle taking in front the Goddess Earth; and the Devas went to Vishnu and began to praise Vishnu Janardana, the Deva of the Devas, with the words of the Vedas with full devotion.
Brahma said Thou hast thousand heads, thousand faces, thousand feet. Thou art the Purusha of the Vedas, Thou art the Deva of the Devas, and Thou art Eternal.
O Omnipresent! Thou art the Past, Present, and Future! O Lord of Lakshmi! Thou hast awarded immortality unto us.
Thou art the Creator of universe, the Preserver and the Destroyer; Thou art the One and the Only goal and thou art the God. Everybody knows that all these glories belong to Thee.
Vyasa said O king! When Brahma praised thus, Vishnu whose sign was Garuda, was highly pleased and appeared before Brahma and the other Devas.
The Bhagavan asked them about their welfare and enquired in detail into the cause of their arrival there.
Brahma them bowed down to Him and, remembering the cause of the sorrows of the Goddess Earth, said O Lord! Thou art now to relieve the burden of the Earth.
O Thou, Ocean of mercy! When the end of the Dvapara yuga will come Thou art to incarnate in the world and kill the wicked kings and thus to relieve the burden of the Earth.

Vishnu said I am not independent in these matters; why I? Brahma Mahesha, Indra, Agni, Yama, Visvakarma, the Sun and Varuna and other Devas, nobody is independent. This whole universe, moving and unmoving is existing under the control of the Yoga Maya; and from Brahma up to the clot of grass, all are strung into the thread of Her Three qualities.

O One of good vows! Whatever that Yoga Maya, the Supreme Goddess, Who is All will. Whose mouth is inward. Who does good at all times, what She wills She does that at any time. You should all know that we are entirely under Her control.

You better think that were I independent, what for would I have stayed in the great ocean, incarnating in the Fish and Tortoise Bodies! O Brahmin! What name or pleasure is there in enjoyment in the body of lower animals! What holy merit or any other reward may I expect from being born in the wombs of lower animals? What is the reason that I assume the body of a Boar? or of a Man-Lion? or of a Dwarf? Why was I born as the son of Jamadagni. Especially why did I, being born of that highsouled Brahman Jamadagni, and being the best of the Brahmins, do the most atrocious act like that of a heartless brute and fill up the lakes with their blood. Alas! I killed the Ksatriyas mercilessly; to say nothing more than that I killed the sons

that were then in the wombs. Were I independent, what for I would have done these horrible and cruel deeds! O Lord of the Devas! See again. In my Rama incarnation I roamed on foot, helpless and without any provision, in the fearful Dandaka forest unfrequented by anybody, wearing clotted hair, bark, rags, like a man who feels no shame, and behaved like a hunter and killed many animals.
